data.text: Make the ddflow tool to prioritize the fixing of the bugs by default in front of features so the bugs are not affecting the feature development. Unless the user asks something else, by default the bugs should be prioritized to be fixed

data.title: Bugs are offered before features by default

data.body: Operator (2026-09-28): prioritize fixing bugs ahead of features by default so bugs do not affect feature development, unless the operator asks otherwise. plan() orders the ready set by (not-a-bug, priority, id) when [schedule] bugs_first = true (default). An item is a bug when tagged with a [flow] bugfix_tags/hotfix_tags tag, or named by an OPEN bug record (bug found --item). The parallelism cap therefore hands its slots to bugs first. bugs_first = false restores pure priority order. Test: a bug at priority 100 is offered before a feature at priority 10; off-switch restores priority order; a fixed bug record no longer promotes its item.
data.title: Offer bug fixes before features by default ([schedule] bugs_first)

data.summary: task add (and phase add) silently overwrite an EXISTING item with the same id in the same log: api.items.task_add checks only port ids for a clash, never the id itself. Seen live 2026-09-28: B207 (bugs-first scheduling, lamport 695) was replaced by another agent's 'task add B207' (companions fix, lamport 728) — title, globs, body all replaced, no error, no warning; the operator's task vanished from the queue. Probe: ddflow task add X1 --phase P --title a; ddflow task add X1 --phase P --title b -> exit 0, show X1 says 'b'. Expected: refuse (exit 3) naming the existing item and suggesting a free id.

data.claim: No: plan() sorts the ready set by (priority, id) only, so a bug at the default priority 100 is offered after a feature at 10, and under a cap of one slot the bug is withheld entirely. Every consumer (next, brief, claim suggestions) reads plan().ready, so one sort key covers them all.

data.summary: 'ddflow update <ID> --globs' does not widen a HELD lease, though the pre-commit hook's own remedy says it does ('ddflow update <ID> --globs ...  # widen an existing claim'). The item's globs change; lease.globs stays as claimed, so the hook keeps warning (would refuse under commit_without_lease=block) and anything that conflict-checks against lease globs does not see the new path. Seen 2026-09-28 on B-bugs-first: update added ddflow/templates/prompts/help/parallel.md; show --json -> item globs has it, lease globs does not; commit hook warned 'not covered by a lease you hold'. data.summary: 'ddflow bug fixed <id>' accepts an id that names no recorded bug and reports success: api.knowledge.bug_fixed (parameter misleadingly named 'item') appends bug.fixed for any subject and _h_bug_fixed setdefault()s a phantom Bug. Passing the TASK id (natural, since bug found --item links one) prints 'bug REC closed', fabricates a closed bug REC, and leaves the real bug open. Probe: bug found --item REC --summary x; bug fixed REC --regression-test t.py -> exit 0 'bug REC closed'; the auto-id bug is still open. Expected: refuse (exit 3) naming the open bugs linked to REC.

evidence.note: Scratch repo probes via real CLI: default next -> [FIX(tag bug), REC(open bug record), FEAT(prio 10)]; [schedule] bugs_first=false in config.toml -> [FEAT, FIX, REC] (not silently dropped; 'ddflow config' shows it [file]); DDFLOW_SCHEDULE_BUGS_FIRST=true overrides; empty bug set -> key constant, pre-change order. Found pre-existing bug: 'bug fixed <task id>' fabricates a closed phantom bug (filed); B-bugs-first behaves correctly there (real bug still open, item stays promoted).

data.body: api.items.task_add checks only generated port ids for a clash, never the id itself; phase_add likewise. 2026-09-28: B207 (the operator's bugs-first task) was replaced by another agent's task add B207 - title, globs, body - with exit 0. Also the root cause of the cross-family critic's finding on B-bugs-first: an open bug record naming an overwritten id promotes the unrelated new item. Fix: refuse (exit 3) naming the existing item (title, holder) and suggest a free id; a REMOVED item's id may be re-added only with an explicit flag. Regression test must fail on unfixed code. Check import/replay paths that may legitimately re-emit task.added.
